tagline: Up the glacier-cut canyon that built the Salt Lake Temple.
intro: SR-210 turns into the mouth of Little Cottonwood Canyon a few minutes from downtown Salt Lake City and climbs east through a corridor the glaciers carved. Granite walls 400 feet high rise beside the road, known the world over for crack climbing. The road passes Snowbird and ends at Alta, one of the highest towns in Utah at 8,950 feet.
It is the smaller of the two Cottonwood canyons, which is the whole reason for its name. It is also part of Salt Lake City's watershed, so pets stay home.

moments.title: Granite Mountain
moments.text: A mile up stands a mass of rock that is mostly quartz monzonite despite its name, the same stone as the Salt Lake Temple, with a church records vault dug 600 feet into it.

moments.title: Snowbird
moments.text: A resort opened in December 1971 on old Emma Mine ground, a mine sold to British investors in 1871 at an inflated price that ended with an American ambassador recalled.

moments.title: Alta
moments.text: By the 1930s the old silver camp was down to one resident, George Watson, who gave his land to the Forest Service on condition that it become a ski area.

practical: The canyon is in the Salt Lake City watershed. No pets are allowed, and swimming and wading are prohibited.
